NEW MOON IN SCORPIO ♏️🌑

The second New Moon of fall arrives tonight, November 8, at 11:02 PM Pacific, bringing us face-to-face with our fears, buried emotions, and the things we’ve allowed to have power over us for far too long.

Scorpio doesn’t allow us to comfortably ignore what’s happening beneath the surface. This New Moon asks us to confront some uncomfortable truths about ourselves, our relationships, and what we’ve continued to tolerate long after knowing better.

With the New Moon squaring Mars in Leo, frustrations are running HIGH. We may feel ready to confront people, make drastic changes, or finally say what’s been on our minds. But with Mercury and Venus still retrograde until November 13, I encourage you to think before reacting. Not every situation requires an immediate response.

This New Moon is about taking our power back. We cannot undo the past, but we can decide how much longer we’re willing to let it dictate our lives.

For your magical work tonight, consider what you’ve been holding onto out of fear, and what needs to change.

After 13 years of The Hoodwitch, I think it’s fair to say that I innovated an entirely new visual language and style of storytelling that has influenced a generation of witches, creatives, influencers, brands, and even television series.

Looking back at these images, from my Vogue feature with marjon_carlos to my refinery29 installation, I’m reminded of just how much of what you see in the world of modern witchcraft today has been influenced by the work I’ve created over the years. The photography, the imagery, the aesthetics, the way we tell stories about magic. I’ve watched so much of it become part of the mainstream.

I’ve loved watching my own work evolve, too. From my early obsession with crystals and beautiful altars to exploring my shadow, confronting the uncomfortable parts of myself, and developing a much deeper relationship with my magical practice. I’ve grown up alongside The Hoodwitch, and the work has grown with me. This is my Scorpio baby 🥹

I don’t claim to have invented witchcraft (Obviously) 🤣 but  I do know what I’ve contributed to its visual culture, and after 13 years, I’m not going to pretend otherwise.

I’m incredibly proud of what I’ve built, the doors I’ve opened, and the people I’ve inspired along the way.

Anyway, check your inboxes tomorrow. Those invoices are LONG overdue. 💋

Xo, Bri

October 26–November 1

Halloween week begins with the Taurus Full Moon bringing our desires into focus. We may be craving more affection, more stability, or enough peace to enjoy what we already have. Pay attention to what feels worth your time and what has become exhausting to maintain.

With Mercury and Venus both retrograde, unfinished conversations may find their way back to us. I’ve been thinking a lot about this over the past few days, especially after celebrating 13 years of The Hoodwitch on Friday.

How much of our lives we spend collecting things…
People, places, memories, experiences, books, music, photographs, friendships, heartbreaks, and all the different versions of ourselves we’ve had to become along the way. 

Some things we outgrow or lose. Some things we carry with us forever, but looking  back at the last 13 years, I can see pieces of every version of myself in the work I’ve created. The things I was obsessed with, people who inspired me, lessons i’ve learned, and even the things I no longer believe in.

I think there’s something really beautiful about being able to look back at your life and recognize just how much you’ve loved, destroyed, created, and changed.

Nothing we genuinely love ever leaves us entirely. It becomes part of our history and a part of who we are. ❤️🌹

♐️ WELCOME TO SAGITERRORIST SEASON. 🏹

November 22 – December 21.

The Sun has officially entered Sagittarius, the ninth sign of the zodiac, ruled by Jupiter, the planet of expansion, philosophy, wisdom, and occasionally, an absolutely outrageous amount of confidence.

In mythology, Sagittarius is represented by the archer, a half-human, half-horse figure pointing an arrow toward the heavens. The symbolism speaks to our eternal pursuit of knowledge, truth, and something greater than ourselves.

I’ve always found it interesting that Sagittarius is associated with Temperance, a card representing moderation, patience, and restraint, considering Sagittarians are notoriously convinced that their opinions are universal truths But maybe that’s the whole point. Temperance represents the very lessons Sagittarius is here to learn.

This Sagittarius season is anything but quiet. With Uranus activated in Gemini, unexpected information, sudden revelations, and changing circumstances may disrupt what we thought we knew. The next several weeks challenge us to question our beliefs, reconsider our assumptions, and recognize where we’ve mistaken certainty for understanding.

✨Read your Sagittarius season horoscope and discover what the coming weeks have in store for your sign at TheHoodwitch.com

🕯️Feliz Día de Muertos 🖤

Today, I celebrate my loved ones, those who came before me, whose sacrifices, wisdom, and love continue to live through me.

Día de Muertos is NOT the “Mexican Halloween”. it is a sacred celebration of life, death, and remembrance. Through our ofrendas, candles, Cempasúchil, prayers, and favorite foods, we honor our beloved dead with gratitude and joy.

Today, my heart also grieves for the innocent lives that have been lost in ICE custody and the families torn apart by detention and deportation. Those who have died were not merely statistics. They were human beings with names, families, histories, and people who loved them very much. They deserve remembrance, dignity, and justice.

Our dead are never forgotten as long as we continue to speak their names.

In 2018, we shared the true history and Indigenous origins of Día de Muertos. Read “The Truth Behind Día de los Muertos” at TheHoodwitch.com 

Para nuestros muertos, con todo nuestro amor. 🕯️❤️

✦ Do you harvest and dry your own herbs?

Rosemary, thyme and sage can be tied into small bundles and hung somewhere warm, dry and airy. 

Gather them on a dry day, once the dew has lifted, and let them dry fully before storing them in labelled jars. 

Then they’re ready to reach for in your cooking, spells or seasonal rituals.

The photography, the imagery, the aesthetics, the way we tell stories about magic. I’ve watched so much of it become part of the mainstream.

I’ve loved watching my own work evolve, too. From my early obsession with crystals and beautiful altars to exploring my shadow, confronting the uncomfortable parts of myself, and developing a much deeper relationship with my magical practice. I’ve grown up alongside The Hoodwitch, and the work has grown with me. This is my Scorpio baby 🥹

I don’t claim to have invented witchcraft (Obviously) 🤣 but  I do know what I’ve contributed to its visual culture, and after 13 years, I’m not going to pretend otherwise.

They told you Harry Potter is just a children’s story. They told you the magic is harmless. They told you the books are about friendship and courage.

But what if Harry Potter was inspired by demonic practices — and this is proof?

Here’s what they don’t tell you:

✅ The spells are real — Avada Kedavra. Crucio. Imperio. These are not random sounds. They echo real Latin and Hebrew roots used in older grimoires. The books teach children how to speak them with power and intention. Fiction is the packaging. The language is older than the books.

✅ The occult connection — Ask people deep in the occult what their favorite childhood story was. Harry Potter comes up again and again. The Sorting Hat. The houses. The wands. The bloodlines. It plants the idea that magic is normal, power is inherited, and dark forces can be controlled if you are special enough. That is how the gate opens.

✅ The disguise — The movies made it beautiful. The music made it emotional. Millions of children repeated the spells out loud. They wore the symbols. They joined the houses. They learned that witchcraft is exciting and rebellion is heroic. A generation grew up thinking the occult is just entertainment. Entertainment is the perfect disguise.

Would you rather visit your ancestors in the past or meet your descendants in the future? 

October and November are months of ancestral veneration. We tend our altars, prepare offerings, and spend time honoring our dead. This year, Venus retrograde in Scorpio brings questions of love and inheritance into that practice. Some of the beliefs we’re reconsidering have been in our families longer than anyone can remember.

With Mercury also in Scorpio, I’m interested in what we could learn if we could hear the stories firsthand. Family history changes depending on who is telling it. There are things people take to the grave that everyone else spends a lifetime trying to understand.

If you could sit down with an ancestor, what would you actually ask? Would you want to know how they practiced their magic? Who taught them? Would you tell them what happened to their children or homes? 

I wonder what they would make of us. Would they recognize something they had prayed for, or have some serious questions about what the hell we’re doing. 

Meeting our descendants would put us on the other side of that conversation. We would be answering questions about our beliefs, our choices, and things we never imagined anyone would remember.

That feels like a question worth sitting with this ancestor season. Would you go back, or would you go forward? 🤔🤔

esoteric.caption:
The temples have fallen silent. The priesthoods have vanished. Empires have risen from dust and returned to it. Yet the current of the Ancient Wisdom has never ceased to flow.

From the shadowed sanctuaries of Egypt, where the mysteries of divine kingship, cosmic order, and the perfection of the soul were first clothed in symbol and ritual, there emerged a tradition not bound to any single creed or civilization. The outward forms changed with the centuries — pagan, Christian, Enlightenment, and secular, but the inner doctrine endured.

Freemasonry stands as one of the great vessels of that continuity. Neither a religion nor a relic of the past, it serves as a living repository of initiatic knowledge, preserving through allegory, architecture, geometry, and ceremonial drama those perennial truths once taught within the mystery schools of antiquity. The sacred eye, the pillars, the celestial vault, the working tools of the builder; all are fragments of a language far older than the modern world.

The Pharaoh and the Mason are separated by millennia, yet they stand beneath the same Light. One gazes upon the mysteries through the symbols of Egypt, the other through the symbolism of the Lodge. The garments differ; the wisdom remains.

For while nations, faiths, and philosophies pass through successive ages, the Brotherhood persists as a guardian of the hidden tradition, preserving the ember of ancient knowledge against the darkness of forgetfulness, carrying it from age to age until the seeker is prepared to receive it.

Lux ex Tenebris. Ordo ab Chao.
The forms of civilization change; the Mystery endures.

Let’s make one thing clear from the start. God is everything, but religion, as most people know it, is something constructed. Not divine in its current form, but shaped over time by human hands with power and control in mind. History wasn’t just written, it was edited, filtered, and locked away until truth became distant and almost unrecognizable.

What we live in is not just a world, it’s a curated version of reality. Information was never meant to be fully free, because free information wakes people up. And once people wake up, the illusion begins to crack. That’s why truth is often hidden, complicated, or drowned in noise.

They didn’t just organize society, they divided perception. Borders were drawn not only on maps, but in minds. Countries became enclosures, ideologies became identities, and people forgot what unity feels like. Instead, they were placed into systems where they compete for survival, believing that’s natural.

Meanwhile, those at the top never played the same game. They sit at the table while others fight over crumbs and call it competition. In reality, it’s a controlled structure where distraction keeps most from seeing the bigger picture.

Even spirituality was reshaped. People were taught to pray from a place of weakness, hoping to be saved, instead of understanding their connection to something greater. And a person who believes they are powerless is easier to guide.

If everything broke at once, systems, beliefs, everything people rely on, the truth wouldn’t disappear with it. It would do the opposite. It would surface. Because truth doesn’t depend on structures, only illusions do. And once those structures fail, what’s left is raw understanding. Not comfort, not fear, just clarity that was always there, buried under layers.

What we call truth today is often just an inherited version, passed through generations, translated, adjusted, and reshaped until it fits a certain narrative. Not necessarily false, but not untouched either.

So the real question was never about finding truth. It’s about realizing who shaped the version of truth you’ve been given, and why❓

"Classical Elements refer to Earth, Water, Air, Fire, and Spirit. Ancient cultures such as Greece, Egypt, Persia, Tibet, India, and Japan considered the Classical Elements as the building blocks of the Universe. They used the concept of Elements to explain manifested Creation's complexity and nature in simpler terms. Their lists of the Elements and sequence of manifestation varied slightly but held the same meanings. The Spirit Element was interchangeable with Aethyr, Ether, Void, Akasha, and Space, depending on the tradition. The Chinese Wu Xing system is slightly different since it describes various types of energy in a state of constant flux and interaction with one another, referred to as the "Five Phases" of natural phenomena. The Five Phases of Wu Xing are Wood, Fire, Water, Metal, and Earth. The Chinese Elements are seen as ever-changing and moving, while the Classical Elements are separate from one another even though they are parts of a whole. The Ancients postulated that the outside Universe (Macrocosm), including the energy composition of every human being (Microcosm), consists of the Five Elements. The Five Elements correspond with the Seven Chakras (Figure 9). They comprise our Aura and the Cosmic Planes and Subtle Bodies that our consciousness partakes of. The first four Chakras correspond with Earth, Water, Fire, and Air, while the three higher Chakras correspond with Spirit. The Chakras, in turn, compare with the Sephiroth on the Tree of Life in the Western Mystery Tradition. Their correspondence is complex and not as apparent as many Spiritual teachers believe, but the relationship is there..."CONTINUED IN COMMENTS -Excerpt from "Serpent Rising: The Kundalini Compendium" by Neven Paar

hermeticism.caption: Maymon, Demon King of the South. // According to the Grimoire of St. Cyprian, Maymon is one of the Four Demon Kings, and is attributed to the South. He is associated with a black bird, crowned and standing upon a branch, similar to the illustration found in Faust’s Magia Naturalis et Innaturalis. In Clavis Inferni, Maymon is placed in opposition to the Archangel Gabriel. He is also associated with sovereignty over other spirits, including Asmodeus, who is described as acting under his power. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Egyn, Demon King of the North. // According to the Grimoire of St. Cyprian, Egyn is one of the Four Demon Kings, and is attributed to the North. He is associated with a blue, crowned bear, representing the element of Earth. In Clavis Inferni, Egyn is placed in opposition to the Archangel Uriel. He is associated with knowledge of the natural world, hidden things, and the revelation of secrets. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Fleur-de-lis ankh. // I worked on this piece a few years ago when I first moved to New Orleans. Originally associated with the French monarchy, the fleur-de-lis arrived in Louisiana during the French colonial period and eventually became one of the city’s most recognizable emblems. The ankh symbolizes everlasting life, while the fleur-de-lis evokes New Orleans’ French heritage. The earliest versions of the fleur-de-lis were represented as scarab beetles, which the Egyptians regarded as sacred symbols of rebirth, renewal, and spiritual enlightenment. The two symbols combined celebrate New Orleans as a crossroads of history and spirituality. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Anu, Lord of the Constellations. // Known as the Sky Father, King of the Gods, Lord of the Constellations, Anu is the divine personification of the sky, supreme God and father of all the deities in the Mesopotamian religion. He was believed to be the supreme source of all authority, for the other gods and for all mortal rulers, and he is described in one text as the one “who contains the entire universe”. He is identified with the north ecliptic pole centered in the constellation Draco. His symbol is the Dingir, a star shaped ideogram that represents the heavens. The original association of divinity is thus with the “bright” or “shining” stars in the sky. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Heart, skin, and flesh. // The keys to the construction of the Enochian Lamen are in the condensation of the 12x7 table containing the letters of the names of the seven planetary Heptarchic Kings and their Princes. From the outside in, the Lamen is divided into three sections: the flesh, heart, and skin. The flesh is added to the perimeter of the Lamen, then the heart to the corners of the inner square. The skin is added to the corners of the diamond square, and the remaining letters of the 12x7 table are woven in between. As the Table of Practice conciliates Heaven and earth, so does the Lamen placed over the heart conciliate the magician to the Holy Table. // Gold, link in profile.

ATHENA PARTHENOS. // Athena Parthenos represents another aspect of the Divine Feminine. As Parthenos, the Virgin, Athena belongs to herself. Her virginity can be understood not simply as the absence of sexuality, but as independence and self-possession. She represents wisdom, craftsmanship, protection, and strength. Her power comes from knowing when to create, when to protect, and when to fight. The statue represented Athena as the patron goddess and protector of Athens, embodying wisdom, warfare, and the authority of the city, and is reflected in Athena’s relationship with weaving. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Yale has a secret. And it’s been locked behind marble walls for 60 years 🕯️

Inside one of the most prestigious universities in America sits a collection of over 300 medieval and Renaissance manuscripts on the dark arts. The kind of books medieval kings would have killed for. The kind of books the Catholic Church tried to burn. The kind of books most people don’t even know exist.

Spells to turn lead into gold. Instructions for summoning spirits. Recipes for the legendary Philosopher’s Stone. Original alchemy notes by Sir Isaac Newton, who spent more of his life chasing magic than he did chasing physics.
It’s called The Mellon Alchemy Collection. And it got there because of one woman.

In the 1940s, Mary Mellon, the wife of one of America’s wealthiest men, fell down a rabbit hole. After meeting psychiatrist Carl Jung, she became obsessed with alchemy and began quietly buying up some of the rarest occult manuscripts on Earth. When she died at just 41 years old, her husband Paul donated her entire collection to Yale in her memory.

Today it lives inside the Beinecke Rare Book Library, a six-story marble tower of books so precious that rumor has it the building will suffocate anyone inside if a fire ever breaks out — to save the manuscripts first.

The best part? Yale digitized almost all of it. You can read books medieval rulers killed people for. From your couch. For free.

Your move 🕯️
Save this for your next 2AM rabbit hole.
